title: Rebook parking and claim the refund with an agent
summary: When a garage was full before a Broadway show, the author's phone agent booked a nearby spot in two minutes and later won a refund using an emailed receipt.
agent_role: The agent found and paid for a replacement spot, filed the refund request, and pulled the receipt from email to answer the app's proof request. The human only opened the agent and made the initial ask.
outcome: Author reports the new spot was booked within two minutes and the refund arrived three days later, with no typing on their part.
what_they_did: The poster had booked parking ahead for a Broadway show, but the garage was full. They opened an AI agent on their phone. It booked and paid for a spot a few blocks away. During the show it asked the parking app for a refund. When the app wanted proof, it found the new receipt in their email and sent it.
how_it_went: The author says the new spot took about two minutes to book. The refund arrived three days later. They say they didn't type a word.
worth_knowing: The post does not name the agent or say how it was linked to payments and email. That access is what made the hands-off refund possible.
prompt: The parking I booked at [garage name] for [date/time] fell through. Find available parking within [distance] of [destination] for [duration] under [budget]. Show me the top 3 options and wait for my approval before booking or paying. After I park, draft a refund request to [original parking app] explaining the garage was full. If they ask for proof, find the new parking receipt in my email and show me the reply before sending it.

curation.rationale: A genuine multi-step daily-life errand: the agent rebooked parking, filed a refund claim and answered a proof request using an emailed receipt. It is a short first-hand anecdote with no named product or setup details; daily-life boost applied.
